reviews.title: Beware of the Platform Rules & Credit System
reviews.text:
I joined DateMyAge hoping to meet people closer to my age and was initially impressed by how engaged and communicative many of the men seemed. Within five days, however, I had already spent about $109 between the membership and additional credits.

The biggest issue for me is the credit-based communication system. Regular chats use credits, emails can cost 10 credits just to open, and other features cost even more. I also learned that “Free Users” are encouraged to stay very active and responsive on the platform, which made me question how much of the constant attention was organic versus influenced by the structure of the site.

I had several conversations that became unusually intense very quickly, with frequent follow-ups and repeated attempts to keep the conversation going. When I asked one person I had genuinely enjoyed talking with whether he would be open to moving our conversation off the platform, he preferred to continue chatting there. That was the point where I decided the experience no longer felt comfortable or authentic enough for me to continue paying for.

The app itself functions fine, and I did have some enjoyable conversations, which is why I’m giving it 2 stars rather than 1. But I strongly recommend understanding the credit system and Free User model before spending money here. It can become expensive very quickly.

A point of interest is I was receiving 10-15 messages daily while my subscription was active. I cancelled my subscription less than 24 hours

reviews.title: Too Many Red Flags
reviews.text:
I joined Date My Age hoping to meet real people, but my experience was disappointing.

Many of the conversations felt extremely structured and unnatural, almost as if I was speaking to scripted responses rather than genuine people. The replies came very quickly and often followed the same pattern of questions, which made the interactions feel inauthentic.

What concerned me most was that when I shared my WhatsApp number with two different profiles, I received the exact same response from both accounts: that it was "too early" to exchange numbers and that we should continue talking on the platform. Receiving identical responses from different people felt very strange.

Shortly afterward, I was unable to continue the conversations without purchasing additional credits. This left me feeling that the platform is designed to keep users paying rather than helping them make genuine connections.

I cannot say whether the profiles are real or not, but based on my experience, many interactions felt artificial and heavily restricted by the platform's credit system.

I would not recommend this service to someone looking for authentic communication and meaningful connections.
